originality.rationale: The central new claim is the evaluated long-time variance of a stationary time average in independently resetting Brownian particles with arbitrary stationary correlated fixed-anchor ensembles, including an invariant Green--Kubo coefficient and explicit lattice-versus-Poisson contrast. Primary papers establish one-time reset-current laws or no-reset general initial-condition variance laws but not this combined temporal asymptotic. A related previous Poisson-anchor single-particle result is known and excluded as the asserted novelty. Equivalent general renewal specialization remains possible and requires independent priority review.
residual_risks: Broader renewal/occupation-time theory or other resetting models might imply the specific Green--Kubo coefficient as a specialization; independent priority review remains needed.
This variance theorem does not resolve the 2023 paper's quenched large-deviation third-order transition under correlated anchors.

value.rationale: The stationary time-average precision observable is experimentally natural. The theorem separates nondecaying anchor uncertainty from the universal trajectory-noise correction under stochastic resetting and exhibits strong, exactly quantified suppression of static uncertainty under hyperuniform lattice preparation, without suppressing the leading dynamic coefficient. This is a structural, parameter-wide result rather than an isolated calculation.
